title: Module 11 Misconception Sort
intro: Decide whether each statement is true, false, or depends. These are the misconceptions that cost students points on exams.

items.s: If there is a significant interaction, you should interpret the main effects first.
items.why: A significant interaction means the factors work together, so the main effects can be misleading. Interpret the pattern of cell means first.

items.s: You can have a significant interaction with no significant main effects.
items.why: A crossover pattern can cancel out in the marginal means.

items.s: A main effect for factor A tells you how A affects the outcome at every level of B.
items.why: It tells you the average effect across B. The effect may differ by level of B.

items.s: In a two-factor ANOVA, the same MS within is the denominator for all three F ratios.
items.why: The error term comes from variability within cells.

items.s: Parallel lines on an interaction plot indicate no interaction.
items.why: The effect of one factor is the same at each level of the other.

items.s: Adding a second factor always increases the F for the first factor.
items.why: It can, because the second factor removes variance that would otherwise be error, but only if the new factor accounts for real variability.

items.s: A significant interaction proves that one factor causes the effect of the other.
items.why: It describes dependence in the pattern of means. Causal claims still rely on design and random assignment.
